pages.title: A finite-difference gradient check
pages.text:
A ﬁnite-diﬀerence gradient check
For a parameter coordinate θj,
∂jL ≈ L(θ + ϵej) − L(θ − ϵej)2ϵ .
Use a moderate ϵ: too large gives truncation error, too small gives cancellation error.

pages.title: Rectification of a signed response
pages.text:
Rectiﬁcation of a signed response
ReLU(a) = max(0 , a), ReLU(−2) = 0 , | − 2| = 2.
ReLU retains positive responses and removes negative responses. Absolute value retains
the magnitude of either sign. For a signed edge ﬁlter, these operations therefore treat
opposite edge orientations diﬀerently. The companion’s ﬁtted network instead uses tanh.
Scientiﬁc Computing in Python / 2027 Notes 13 / 17

pages.title: Parameter sharing
pages.text:
Parameter sharing
The same 3 × 3 coeﬃcients act at every valid image position.
This reuses nine
parameters per input/output channel pair. A dense map would assign separate weights to
each input coordinate for each output.
